title_en: Fragment on the Letter to Philemon
author: Severianus of Gabala
occasion: The fragment explains Paul's rhetorical strategy in the opening of the letter to Philemon. Severianus notes that Paul often places an unusual word at the start of a letter to prepare for what he is about to say, and that here, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, he shows the credibility of his appeal through his own worth—his worth being that he is bound.
argument: Severianus observes that in many letters Paul places an unusual word that is preparatory for the argument about to be introduced. In the letter to Philemon, Paul is about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus. He demonstrates the credibility of this appeal through his own worth or claim to consideration. That worth consists in his being bound—his imprisonment. The lowly state of being in chains is what gives his appeal its persuasive force.

outline.move: Severianus explains that Paul, about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, demonstrates the credibility of his appeal through his own worth—his worth being that he is bound.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Severianus notes that Paul often places an unusual word at the start of a letter to prepare for what he is about to say
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐν πολλαῖς ἐπιστολαῖς ξένον τίθησι ῥῆμα τοῦ μέλλοντος εἰσάγεσθαι λόγου κατασκευαστικόν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Severianus notes that in many letters Paul places an unusual word that is preparatory for the argument about to be introduced—not specifically 'at the start of a letter'

_unresolved_facts.claim: he shows the credibility of his appeal through his own worth—his worth being that he is bound
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἀξιοῦν ὑπὲρ Ὀνησίμου τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἀξίᾳ–ἀξία δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ δεδέσθαι–, τὸ ἀξιόπιστον τῆς παρακλήσεως δείκνυσιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: he shows the credibility of his appeal through his own worth—his worth being that he is bound. The Greek ἀξιοῦν means 'to ask/request as a favor' or 'to claim as due,' not simply 'to make a request'; and ἀξία carries the sense of 'claim to consideration' or 'desert' based on status/condition, not 'worth' in a general sense

_unresolved_facts.claim: The lowly state of being in chains is what gives his appeal its persuasive force
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source does not characterize imprisonment as 'lowly' (ταπεινός); it simply states τὸ δεδέσθαι as the fact of his condition without evaluative language about lowliness
